concept: Card game artwork preflight imposition and color management

claims.text: Delano’s card guide requires two files per deck: a multi-page front/read file and a back/common file. A single page suffices for an identical common back. It explicitly says not to gang multiple cards on one page and requires the documents to contain cards in order. (low confidence)
Remove template guides from final artwork: PrintNinja excludes template guidelines, and The Game Crafter warns that an undeleted cut-line layer prints on the product. (high confidence)

PrintNinja describes physical proofs as closer to production than prototypes, but warns that not all components use its offset presses and digitally printed components are not color accurate; identify the process used for each proof component before treating it as a color reference. (low confidence)
Delano prefers high-resolution PDF, offers Adobe joboptions for its PDF specifications, and asks for all links and fonts when native Adobe files are supplied. (low confidence)

The Game Crafter warns that printed colors may look darker than the screen and that it cannot guarantee exact color matching across printings or materials; its documentation identifies humidity, heat, fuser age and toner changes as contributing factors. (medium confidence)

The Game Crafter states that printing/cutting registration can vary by up to 1/8 inch and that component backs are more prone to drift than fronts; this is its published tolerance guidance, not a measured failure rate. (low confidence)

The Game Crafter says its supplied color profile can improve screen-to-print matching but cannot make it perfect; it does not guarantee exact color matching between printings or materials. (low confidence)

MakePlayingCards specifies 36 pixels of bleed on each side at 300DPI; its red dotted line marks the safe area rather than the trim edge. Its poker-size example finishes at 2.5 × 3.5 inches and requires a minimum 822 × 1122-pixel upload at 300DPI. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-18)

Thin uniform borders make cutting drift conspicuous. PrintNinja warns that its 0.125-inch borders can look uneven; The Game Crafter recommends full-bleed backgrounds instead of borders to reduce the visibility of registration errors. (medium confidence)

PrintNinja says a physical game proof may contain digitally printed components that are not color accurate; tuck-box proofs default to digital printing. Its proof should therefore be assessed component by component rather than treating an assembled sample as a color reference for every part. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-28)

Delano specifies 100% black only for black text and warns against Registration Black; its recommended rich black for large black areas is 60% cyan, 40% magenta, 40% yellow and 100% black. This recipe is a Delano instruction rather than a universal profile. (low confidence)

The Game Crafter advises against dark solid card edges because cutting can chip toner and expose white stock at the edge. It recommends textures or gradients rather than solid backgrounds. (low confidence)

Superior POD permits individual-card artwork or its 18-up sheets. For the illustrated sheet layout, front-sheet left columns correspond to back-sheet right columns; its example reverses each row from A B C to C B A. Apply this to that supplied layout rather than assuming it fits every press path. (low confidence)

PrintNinja specifies a document at quoted trim size, background bleed of .125 inch on all four sides, and a .125-inch inward safety margin. Delano also specifies final-size documents with 1/8-inch bleed and margins. These are the respective manufacturers’ setup rules. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-28)

For a deck with one common back, PrintNinja prefers one multi-page PDF with one card face per page, one copy of the common back, and every front including duplicate designs. It recommends Back/Front order reflecting the desired deck stack. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-28)

For multiple common backs, PrintNinja accepts one PDF placing each common back before its associated faces, or separate PDFs beginning with each common back; the separate-file route requires communicating final card order to prepress. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-28)

PrintNinja describes imposition as arranging individual pages or cards on parent sheets with operator software. For playing cards, card dimensions and stock-specific parent-sheet sizes determine how many cards fit; a single fixed cards-per-sheet assumption is therefore inappropriate for its different formats and stocks. (low confidence)

Upload color mode depends on the manufacturing workflow: PrintNinja directs customers to export CMYK, whereas The Game Crafter says its website accepts only RGB and rejects CMYK, while recommending CMYK design followed by RGB conversion. These are attributed vendor requirements, not a universal CMYK-upload rule. (high confidence)

The Game Crafter supplies a color profile for use in image editors and recommends it for closer screen-to-print matching. It presents the profile as an improvement, not a promise of perfect matching. (medium confidence)

For horizontally used cards whose two sides should read in the same direction, The Game Crafter instructs customers to rotate either the front or back image by 180 degrees; the instruction does not apply to vertically used cards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2022-11-22)

PrintNinja’s file checklist calls for page count and trim dimensions matching the quote, 300dpi images, and separate files for specialty options such as foil, embossing, debossing and spot UV. Its card guide also says to remove template guidelines before submission. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-28)

Delano’s card template prefers a 3/16-inch safe zone and requires at least 1/8 inch; it says the trim can wander approximately 1/16 inch in any direction. Those numbers describe Delano’s guide, not a measured tolerance for every printer. (low confidence)

PrintNinja specifies a document at the quoted trim size, .125-inch bleed on every edge with backgrounds extended through it, and a .125-inch interior safety margin; PDF export must include document bleed settings. (low confidence)

MakePlayingCards distinguishes bleed from safe area: at 300DPI it removes 36 pixels per edge for bleed and marks a further safe area with a red dotted line; keep important content inside that safe area. (low confidence)
PrintNinja and The Game Crafter warn that thin uniform borders reveal trimming or registration drift; wider borders or borderless artwork reduce its visual impact. (high confidence)
MakePlayingCards provides top, bottom, left and right indicators for both card sides in its online preview so designers can verify front/back orientation. (low confidence)

PrintNinja preflight checks include matching page count and trim size to the quote, supplying 300dpi images, and preparing separate files for specialty operations such as foil stamping, embossing, debossing and spot UV. (low confidence)
